text:
Alex M.: Heads up — seeing a short eviction wave in eu-west1 spot GPU pool causing a bunch of pods to bounce and a noticeable tail-latency spike in inference. :warning:
InfraBot: ALERT: cluster-eu-west1 / nodepool=spot-gpu-eu - 12 preemptible GPU nodes evicted in 3m (autoscaler triggered fallback).
autoscaler-bot: scale decision: prefer provisioned-on-demand fallback (gpunode-fallback-on-demand) — 2 nodes requested.
Priya S.: which nodepool exactly? any recent autoscaler or taint changes pushed?
Alex M.: nodepool names: spot-gpu-eu, spot-gpu-eu-2, fallback pool is gpunode-fallback-on-demand. No k8s rollout that I know of, but we did flip the CA expander to "price" yesterday (PR #4821).
Alex M.: quick snapshot: ```kubectl get nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=spot-gpu-eu --show-labels --no-headers | awk '{print $1" " $6}'
gpunode-spot-eu-34e2  cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=spot-gpu-eu
gpunode-spot-eu-8b7a  cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=spot-gpu-eu
...```
Sam K.: oof. I think the expander flip + recent higher sequence lengths meant CA prioritized cheaper spots and delayed fallback. We also still have that taint-sync lag bug where nodes get tainted after pods start deleting, which causes a drain storm.
Sam K.: mitigation idea: revert expander to "binpack" (or balanced) for eu, increase fallback warm nodes to +3, and reduce CA --scale-down-unneeded-time to 2m for this pool.
Liu Q.: running quick inventory: ```gcloud compute instances list --filter="name~'gpunode-spot-eu'" --zones=eu-west1* --format="value(name,status,zone)"
gpunode-spot-eu-34e2 RUNNING eu-west1-b
gpunode-spot-eu-8b7a TERMINATED eu-west1-c
gpunode-spot-eu-9c1f PREEMPTED eu-west1-d
```
Priya S.: cost note — increasing warm on-demand buffer will add ~3-4k/mo for eu-west1 if we keep it 24/7. Can we do scheduled warm windows instead of full-time?
Alex M.: short-term: I'll revert expander and bump fallback to +2 immediately. Sam, can you open a rollback PR for the expander flip? Priya, we should simulate cost impact in cost dashboard first.
Sam K.: reopening PR now: #4876 (revert expander change) — will request patch to set CA flag --max-node-provision-time=15m as well (we saw long provisioning causing double-scheduling).
autoscaler-bot: log snippet: "scale_up: added 2 (gpunode-fallback-on-demand), pending quota check, provisioning start=1718976600"
Priya S.: scheduling note: let's trial a 6h warm window overlap with peak inference (13:00-19:00 UTC) for 48h before committing to 24/7. That should reduce cost delta.
Liu Q.: created incident task and assigned: INFRA-872 — actions: revert expander (Sam), bump fallback pool (Alex), schedule warm window (Priya), run taint-sync probe (Liu). Link: https://redwood-infra/runbooks/spot-fallback
Alex M.: also adding a short-term hook in the preemption handler to delay pod recreation by 30s to let fallback nodes register (prevents instant churn). I'll push a tiny rollout to platform-agent.
Sam K.: test plan: run chaos preempt on 3 nodes in staging with current CA flags + fallback buffer, measure scheduling latency and pod restarts.
Priya S.: make sure to capture tokenized cost estimates and token-per-second throughput so we can correlate cost->QPS.
Liu Q.: assigning oncall rotation to monitor for 2h post-change, will report back. :thumbsup:
Alex M.: thanks — will update thread when revert PR is merged and fallback nodes are healthy.
